passage: For weeks I had been on the edge of the group, always the one who arrived just after the joke. Then on Monday Mehak waved me over. "We're going for golgappa after school, come with us." I said yes so fast it embarrassed me. All day my chest felt light, and I kept smiling at the wall. But somewhere behind the relief there was a small, careful voice: why now? Would they still want me next week? At the golgappa stall I laughed a lot, and I was glad, but I also texted Anjali, my old bench mate, to say I'd still meet her on Saturday as usual. I don't know how long this will last, and I'm not going to pretend I do. I'm Disha, and I think I can enjoy it without throwing everything else away.

qa.q: Where did Mehak invite Disha to go after school?
qa.a: Mehak invited Disha for golgappa after school.

qa.q: What mixed feelings did Disha have after the invitation?
qa.a: Relief, because Disha's chest felt light and Disha kept smiling, and also wariness, because a small careful voice asked why now and whether they would still want Disha next week.

qa.q: How did Disha keep her older friendship safe?
qa.a: Disha texted Anjali to say they would still meet on Saturday as usual, so Disha enjoys the new group without dropping an old friend.

qa.q: How might Anjali feel about the text?
qa.a: Probably glad to be remembered, and reassured that the new group has not replaced Anjali. 🤍

grounding: After weeks on the edge, Disha is invited into the group and feels relief mixed with wariness while keeping her older friend.

passage:
It came three days before the maths exam, when Siddharth had no time for anything. Sunaina, the one everyone in the music group listened to, leaned over the library table. "We're jamming at my place Friday. Come. You're one of us now."
Siddharth had spent six weeks at the edge of that group, laughing at the right moments, waiting. Relief flooded through him. Then, just as quickly, a question: why now? What would they want?
Friday was also when he'd promised to help Varun, his friend since Class 6, revise for the same exam. Varun was struggling.
Siddharth texted Sunaina: "Can't Friday, promised Varun help with maths. Next time?"
He half expected silence.
"Bring Varun," she wrote. "We'll jam after you revise."
Siddharth grinned. But he also noticed he'd been ready to lose them rather than drop Varun, and that felt good too.

qa.q: How many weeks had Siddharth spent at the edge of the group?
What did Siddharth feel when Sunaina invited him?
qa.a: He felt a flood of relief, then wariness, wondering why they asked now and what they would want.

qa.q: Which choice was wise, and why?
qa.a: Siddharth kept his promise to Varun even at the risk of losing the invitation, so joining did not mean dropping an old friend.

qa.q: How might Sunaina see Siddharth's reply?
qa.a: Sunaina seems to respect his loyalty, inviting Varun too instead of taking offence.

grounding: A teen invited into a group after weeks on the edge feels relief and wariness and keeps his loyalty to an old friend.

passage:
The invitation came on a Tuesday, by the auto stand outside their Bengaluru school. Riya-Anne from the dance crew tapped Chandrika's shoulder. "We need one more for the fest. You're in, if you want."
Chandrika had watched that crew for months from the edge of the practice room. Now her knees nearly buckled with relief. She said yes before she'd even thought.
The first practice was fun. The second, one of the girls started mocking Yogesh, who played tabla for the school band, for his old sandals. The others laughed.
Yogesh had been Chandrika's friend since they were little. He'd walked her home every day when she broke her arm.
She felt the old fear of being on the outside again. Then she said, "Don't. He's my friend." The laughter stopped awkwardly.
After practice she walked over to Yogesh and sat with him while he packed his tabla, where everyone could see.

qa.q: Where did Riya-Anne invite Chandrika to join the crew?
qa.a: By the auto stand outside their Bengaluru school.

qa.q: How did Chandrika feel when she was invited in?
qa.a: She felt huge relief, her knees nearly buckling, after months of watching from the edge.

qa.q: What did Chandrika do that kept her values while enjoying the group?
qa.a: She told the girls to stop mocking Yogesh and openly sat with him, keeping her old friend and her values.

qa.q: How might Yogesh feel when Chandrika sits with him in front of everyone?
qa.a: Yogesh probably feels valued and protected, seeing that his friend has not dropped him for the new group.

grounding: A teen invited into a group feels relief mixed with wariness and keeps her old friend and values.
